original_test_intent: Verify the dedicated 16-bit Enabled Core Count 2 field in each applicable Type 4 structure encodes the approved number of firmware-enabled physical cores, is selected consistently by the legacy Enabled Core Count byte and persists after reboot.
original_method: Read raw Type 4 structures, bounds-check the formatted length, extract the Enabled Core Count 2 UINT16 at its defined offset, retain the legacy enabled-count byte, validate both against Core Count 2 and the approved BIOS/fuse core policy, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the extended enabled-core baseline, BIOS/fuse policy, field-selection rules and reboot plan. Raw extraction and consistency validation are automatable.
required_inputs: Applicable SMBIOS revision and minimum formatted length/offset for Enabled Core Count 2
Expected 16-bit enabled-core value per populated socket
Legacy Enabled Core Count selector-to-extended-field rule
Expected Core Count 2 and approved BIOS-disabled/fused-core relationship
Validated raw SMBIOS parser plus approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS/approved topology sources only; do not change core enablement, CPU online state, SMT or firmware.
Do not treat a missing `EnabledCoreCount2` text label as field absence; retain raw structure bytes, formatted length and offset.
Bounds-check before decoding and preserve legacy Enabled Core Count, Enabled Core Count 2 and Core Count 2 together.
Require the enabled extended value to follow approved total-core and BIOS/fuse policy; an OS offline mask alone cannot define it.
Stop on out-of-bounds/unsupported structures, invalid selector or enabled-versus-total relationships, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Extract the raw Enabled Core Count 2 field per socket, validate legacy selection and total-core/policy consistency, and compare before/after reboot.
Do not toggle cores, substitute an OS online count or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve extended enabled-core values, core-disable/fuse policy and selector/total-core rules.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The compact literal token is decoder-dependent and may yield no output even when the field exists or is folded into a normalized label; it cannot establish raw encoding or formatted-length validity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a version- and length-aware raw Type 4 parser to capture legacy Enabled Core Count, Enabled Core Count 2 and Core Count 2, with decoded output retained only as secondary evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The dedicated EnabledCoreCount2 scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Directly decode the 16-bit Enabled Core Count 2 field from each sufficiently long Type 4 record, verify legacy selector use and validate the extended enabled count against Core Count 2 and approved disabled/fused-core policy before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 structures that include Enabled Core Count 2.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, Type 4 formatted length, BIOS core policy, CPU topology and parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Enabled Core Count 2 layout/selection semantics, approved BIOS/CPU core policy and installed parser documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Uses direct raw-field decoding instead of an unreliable display-label grep and adds total-versus-enabled consistency.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Improves coverage by proving the extended field is present, bounded and internally consistent.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Extended enabled-count baseline and selection/core policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS online logical processors do not directly represent this firmware physical-core field and must remain separately scoped.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve fewer enabled than total physical cores for a documented BIOS/fuse configuration, but the exact per-socket relationship must be explicit; absence is not accepted merely because dmidecode normalizes the label.
expected_evidence: Approved SMBIOS field definition, extended enabled/total matrix, BIOS/fuse policy and parser versions
Complete pre-reboot raw Type 4 bytes with socket/handle, formatted length, legacy enabled byte, Enabled Core Count 2 and Core Count 2
Bounds, selector and enabled-not-exceeding-total consistency results
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot raw comparison
Engineer verdict or specification-based not-applicable determination

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The compact field name is resolvable to the standard extended enabled-core member; the defective grep is a command-fit issue, not a semantic source conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A validated raw parser can inspect the field safely; expected values and parser availability are readiness inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Replaces literal-label dependence with raw extended-field evidence and internal consistency checks.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps the canonical field interpretation but requires direct encoding proof and corrects capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Preserves separate coverage from effective Enabled Core Count and prevents substitution of OS online CPUs.

review_improvement: Detects malformed or inconsistent extended enabled-core encoding even when a decoder prints a plausible normalized value.
independent_technical_reasoning: With the layout, expected counts and policy approved, bounds checking, raw decoding, consistency comparison and reboot persistence are software-controlled.
